current_answer: As of 6 October 2026, reviewed public evidence does not establish a broad capability decline across popular deployed models or a confirmed Claude Opus 5.5 regression. OpenAI marked its 5 October Work Mode incident recovered at 02:10 UTC on 6 October, a separate ChatGPT-conversation incident recovered at 00:01, and a multi-product incident recovered at 03:17; its live status page showed all systems operational at the 13:12 check. A same-day Reddit user says ChatGPT on a selected GPT-5.6 Sol High setting felt weaker than two days earlier, with context and reasoning symptoms, but supplied no task trace, exact client, route, or output comparison. This is one report of possible problems after service recoveries, not a confirmed model or account regression. BridgeBench still displays 96.5% launch power on 4 October within its stated 90–110% band; LiveNerf last reports 12/30 collections on 5 October with no post-baseline comparison. Check the exact surface and status, save the task, settings, and response, then replay after recovery against a dated baseline before switching.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: No broad decline is established. Recent OpenAI incidents are marked recovered, while a new user complaint still needs a matched replay.

summary: OpenAI marked a 5 October Work Mode incident recovered at 02:10 UTC on 6 October, a separate conversation incident at 00:01, and a multi-product incident at 03:17. Its status dashboard showed all systems operational at the 13:12 check; these are service records, not quality measurements.

A same-day user reports context and reasoning symptoms on a selected GPT-5.6 Sol High setting. The post includes no prompt, transcript, task artifact, route, exact client, or independently verified served model; replies include counterreports.
Timing makes this a possible post-incident persistence lead, but not evidence that an outage caused a model regression or affected this user’s account.
BridgeBench continues to display a 96.5% Opus 5.5 launch-power score on 4 October, inside its own 90–110% band; the composite includes task performance, tokens, and cost.
LiveNerf last displayed 12/30 collections by 5 October and no post-baseline comparison. Neither Claude tracker tests the GPT-5.6 report.
If a familiar task fails, check the exact surface and status, save the task/settings/response and any displayed model label, then replay after recovery against a dated baseline before switching.
uncertainty: The same-day ChatGPT complaint is one self-reported experience; exact task, surface, account, effective model, route, and output are not independently verifiable.
Provider status is aggregate; a recovered incident and green dashboard do not prove account-level or task-level recovery.
Timing overlap between the complaint and service incidents does not establish cause.
A wider OpenAI status item marked recovered at 08:26 UTC displays earlier 29 September timeline entries, so its start and relation to 6 October activity remain unclear.
BridgeBench combines task performance, tokens, and cost; LiveNerf has no post-baseline comparison result in its latest inspected progress.
Analytics are unavailable; reader visits, return use, sharing, and funding outcomes are unobserved.
freshness_note: Checked 6 October 2026 at 13:12 UTC. Several OpenAI service incidents had been marked recovered; a same-day quality complaint has no task replay receipt. Service availability, user reports, and capability tests remain separate.
